entries.subject: feat(cron): add bin/refresh-data.sh for daily KEV + vulns refresh
entries.summary: Lets prod self-update without a dev → rsync deploy. Runs app:kev:refresh, app:vulns:rebuild-toc, then a best-effort IndexNow ping of the vulns landing pages and sitemap.

entries.subject: fix(seo): give every BreadcrumbList ListItem an item URL
entries.summary: Google Search Console flagged "Missing field 'item' (in 'itemListElement')" on STIG and SCAP detail pages. Both templates emitted a position-2 ListItem (the title-level breadcrumb) with only a name — schema.org/Google requires an item URL on every entry.

entries.subject: fix(search): link CCI on AP search-result items
entries.summary: The Assessment Procedures section on /search/<query> renders each row as "<AP acronym> · <CCI id>". The AP acronym side stays as a plain ident pill (there's no AP detail page to link to), but the CCI side should deep-link to /cci#CCI-XXXXXX so the existing cci_app.applyHashFilter() pre-filters the catalog table on arrival.

entries.subject: feat(footer): CISA sync badge + refreshed KEV catalog
entries.summary: Adds a third line to the footer status column — "CISA sync · DD MMM YYYY" — sitting below the existing DISA and NIST sync timestamps. Source is the file mtime of the local KEV mirror at resources/data/kev/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json, which app:kev:refresh rewrites every time it runs (and ship.sh calls that on every deploy).

entries.subject: polish: CCI links + mobile layout pass on STIG compare and RMF views
entries.summary: Two interleaved fixes from a post-release audit on /rmf/4, /rmf/5, /search, and /stig/{title}/{v1}/{r1}/{v2}/{r2}.

entries.subject: fix(vulns): rework landing stat row — actionable metrics, 6 cards wide
entries.summary: The original stat row had a "Patch deadlines" card showing "1,573 overdue today · 14 due in next 30 days" — structurally misleading because most KEV entries were added months or years ago, their 2-week BOD 22-01 deadlines passed long ago, and the count trends toward total-catalog-size by definition. The metric only moves with the calendar, not with anyone's actual patching progress.

entries.subject: feat(ops): app:stig:rebuild meta-command + ship.sh KEV/vulns automation
entries.summary: Two operational tightenings around the new /vulnerabilities tree:

entries.subject: feat(vulns): /vulnerabilities tree — CISA KEV + STIG/SCAP IAVM harvest
entries.summary: A new Library section that joins the public CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to the cross-references already living in the STIG and SCAP corpus. Six routes on the web side, six matching JSON endpoints under /api/vulns.

entries.subject: feat(license): adopt AGPL-3.0-or-later + publish /terms page
entries.summary: Drops the "proprietary" placeholder license that came in by default and puts the project under the GNU Affero General Public License (v3 or later) — same family as Mastodon, Nextcloud, and Plausible. The network-copyleft clause means anyone running a modified version of cyber.trackr.live as a public service has to publish their changes under the same license; in practice this discourages closed-source forks while keeping the code legitimately open.

entries.subject: fix(seo): cache-bust local assets via ?v={{ app_version }}
entries.summary: Apache on prod sends `cache-control: max-age=2592000` (30 days) for static assets. Without a per-deploy version query string, returning visitors on aggressive caches (notably Chrome on mobile) keep stale JS and CSS for up to a month after a ship — manifested last as the theme menu button silently breaking on prod after a deploy.

entries.subject: feat(seo): bin/submit-urls.sh for weekly IndexNow bulk submission
entries.summary: Pulls the live sitemap (https://cyber.trackr.live/sitemap.xml), extracts every <loc>, auto-discovers the IndexNow key file from /public/, and POSTs the whole lot to the shared IndexNow endpoint at api.indexnow.org. Bing, Yandex, Seznam, Naver, and DuckDuckGo all get the notification in one call.

entries.subject: feat(deploy): bin/fix-perms.sh — standard PHP-site permissions
entries.summary: After rsync the perms can drift (especially on DreamHost where the remote user shell sometimes carries umask quirks), and Symfony gets cranky about world-writable cache dirs or files it can't read.

entries.subject: feat(deploy): bin/ship.sh for the dev-side push to prod
entries.summary: Companion to bin/deploy.sh.

entries.subject: feat(seo): IndexNow pinger + bin/deploy.sh
entries.summary: IndexNow lets us push URL-change notifications directly to Bing / Yandex / Seznam / Naver / DuckDuckGo (Google opted out of the protocol but has its own faster path via Search Console). Search engines re-fetch flagged URLs within minutes instead of waiting on the natural crawl cycle, which for a content site that updates with every DISA sync is a meaningful win.

entries.subject: fix(seo): per-page meta descriptions, content-driven where possible
entries.summary: Bing flagged duplicate-template descriptions across pages.

entries.subject: refresh changelog snapshot
fix(changelog): freeze command + JSON fallback for rsync deploys
entries.summary: Production is rsynced from dev — no .git directory survives the copy — so the original Changelog service that shelled out to git log fell back to the empty state on prod. /changelog showed only the "check the GitHub history instead" message instead of any real entries.

entries.subject: feat(seo): dynamic sitemap.xml + flat /stig/index for crawler depth
entries.summary: The static sitemap captured a snapshot from October 2023 — 971 URLs, missing every STIG / SCAP version added since plus the entire feature set shipped this iteration (plans, ckl-viewer, baselines, r4-to-5, changelog, atom feed). Replaces it with a controller-rendered sitemap that walks the toc files at request time so it stays current without any rebuild step.

entries.subject: feat(changelog): /changelog page sourced from git log + footer link
entries.summary: Reverse-chronological list of every commit in the project's history, generated at request time directly from git so it's always current without any rebuild step. Linked from the footer About column between Mission and Contact.

entries.summary: The README still reflected the pre-plan-generator era. Substantial features have shipped since: 20-family RMF Plan Generator, browser- only CKL/CKLB viewer with SCAP overlay, baseline coverage heat map, r4 ↔ r5 mapping page (with withdrawal targets harvested from r5's own catalog), STIG Digest of Updates + Atom feed, OSCAL-driven multi-baseline overlays (14 profiles across NIST + FedRAMP + CNSSI 1253), saved searches, share button, and per-page Open Graph / Twitter Card / JSON-LD metadata.

entries.subject: feat(nav): share-this-page button in the sticky header
entries.summary: Sits in the right cluster between the site search and the theme menu, matching .theme-toggle's 36px icon-button styling. Clicking shares the current URL — whatever deep-linked page the user is on, a STIG view, a control catalog page, a baseline cell — that exact URL gets shared.

entries.subject: feat(search): saved searches — localStorage-backed bookmarks
entries.summary: Drop-down list of saved queries reachable from the hero search box on the home page and from the /search results page header. Each entry stores the query plus an optional user-supplied label; clicking re-runs the search.

entries.subject: feat(seo): per-page Open Graph + Twitter Card + JSON-LD metadata
entries.summary: Makes link-previews on Slack / LinkedIn / Discord / X / Mastodon / generic OG-aware tools render with real titles, real descriptions, and a 1200×630 image — instead of the URL-as-fallback every previewer otherwise produces. Drives organic discovery without any moderation cost or runtime overhead.

entries.subject: feat(plans): privacy-baseline UX surfaces
entries.summary: The privacy baseline (nist-privacy) was already in the wizard's baseline dropdown — every overlay loaded by OverlayLoader is offered automatically.

entries.subject: feat(rmf): baseline coverage heat map at /baselines
entries.summary: Visualizes 800-53 r5 family-by-baseline distribution as a 20×4 grid: each cell shows how many controls + enhancements that NIST baseline selects from that family, color-tinted by intensity (count / max). Click a cell to see the full control list with deep-links into the catalog detail page; click a family-row label to jump directly to that family in /rmf/5.

entries.subject: fix(ckl): SCAP file picker no longer steals clicks across the page
entries.summary: The SCAP file input had class .ckl-drop__input, which sets position: absolute; inset: 0; width: 100%; height: 100% on the element. Its parent (.ckl-toolbar__right) had no position: relative, so the input climbed to the next positioned ancestor — in practice covering most of the page with an invisible click target.

entries.subject: feat(ckl): browser-only CKL/CKLB viewer + editor + SCAP overlay + CKLB export
entries.summary: Drop a STIG checklist in any DISA-supported format, read it on a polished dashboard, edit every assessor-facing field, optionally apply a SCAP XCCDF scan to auto-update statuses, and export the result as a modern CKLB JSON that DISA STIG Viewer 3.x reads natively. All processing is client-side — no checklist data ever leaves the browser.

entries.summary: Public site, public internet — users must explicitly confirm before launching any plan generator that they will not enter classified data or CUI. Bootstrap modal triggered on every plan-card click; gated by a checkbox the user must tick before the Continue button activates.

entries.subject: feat(plans): PM family plan — ALL 17 FAMILIES SHIP
entries.summary: Program Management — closes Tier 4 alongside PL, SR, PT, and closes the entire Tier 1-4 plan rollout (17 of 17 families). PM is structurally distinct: NIST treats PM controls as organizational, not system-level; PM is not in any LMH baseline (always-required, selected separately).

entries.subject: feat(plans): PT family plan (PII Processing and Transparency)
entries.summary: PT — third Tier 4 family. r5-only privacy family with 8 base controls + 13 enhancements.

entries.subject: feat(plans): SR family plan (Supply Chain Risk Management)
entries.summary: Supply Chain Risk Management — second Tier 4 family. r5-only family (no r4 predecessor) — extends RA-3(1) into a formal C-SCRM program per NIST SP 800-161 r1.

entries.subject: feat(plans): PL family plan — Tier 4 starts
entries.summary: Planning — first Tier 4 family. Meta-family: documents how the SSP itself, the Rules of Behavior, security and privacy architectures, baseline selection (FIPS 199 / 200), and baseline tailoring are governed.

entries.subject: feat(plans): AT family plan — Tier 3 COMPLETE
entries.summary: Awareness and Training — closes Tier 3 alongside PE, PS, MA, MP. The smallest 800-53 family at moderate (4 base controls + AT-2(2) / AT-2(3) in baseline).

entries.subject: feat(plans): MP family plan (Media Protection)
entries.summary: Media Protection — fourth Tier 3 family. Compact at moderate (7 base controls, no in-baseline enhancements) but the rigor is in classification-driven handling, sanitization-decision discipline (NIST SP 800-88 r1 Decision Tree), and chain-of-custody for transport.

entries.subject: feat(plans): MA family plan (Maintenance)
entries.summary: Maintenance — third Tier 3 family. Compact at moderate (6 base controls + MA-3(1)/(2)/(3) in baseline) but the rigor is in vendor escort, sanitization-before-vendor-maintenance, and nonlocal-maintenance session protections (bastion, JIT, recording).

entries.subject: feat(plans): PS family plan (Personnel Security)
entries.summary: Personnel Security — second Tier 3 family. Smallest family in 800-53 r5: 9 base controls and no enhancements at moderate.

entries.subject: feat(plans): PE family plan — Tier 3 starts
entries.summary: Physical and Environmental Protection — first Tier 3 family. Distinctive in being heavily inheritance-driven for cloud-hosted systems: each guided control carries an explicit `<control>_inherited` extra field so the plan documents the inheritance posture rather than implying implementation.

entries.subject: feat(plans): SA family plan — Tier 2 COMPLETE
entries.summary: System and Services Acquisition — closes Tier 2 alongside SC and RA. Renders 101 cards at nist-moderate (11 bases + 90 enhancements — the SA family carries 33 SA-8 enhancements and 12 SA-15 enhancements single-handedly) with 90 ODV inputs and 90 disposition pickers; 38 KB DOCX with valid OOXML.

entries.subject: feat(plans): RA family plan (Risk Assessment)
entries.summary: Risk Assessment — second Tier 2 family. Methodology-heavy and smaller than SC: 6 base controls in nist-moderate, but the engineering work is process documentation (categorization, methodology, risk register, acceptance authority) rather than tooling sprawl.

entries.subject: feat(plans): SC family plan — Tier 2 starts
entries.summary: System and Communications Protection — the largest technical family in 800-53 r5. Renders 91 cards at nist-moderate (18 bases + 73 enhancements) with 74 ODV inputs and 73 disposition pickers; 36 KB DOCX with valid OOXML.

entries.subject: feat(plans): CA family plan — Tier 1 COMPLETE
entries.summary: Eighth family on the Phase 2 baseline. The meta family — every other plan's §7 already references CA-7 (Continuous Monitoring); this plan defines the strategy.

entries.subject: feat(plans): SI family plan (System and Information Integrity)
entries.summary: Seventh family on the Phase 2 baseline. Pairs with AU (SI-4 monitoring feeds the audit pipeline), IR (SI-3 malware + SI-7 integrity findings generate incident signals), and RA (SI-2 flaw remediation consumes RA-5 vulnerability scans).

entries.subject: feat(plans): CP family plan (Contingency Planning)
entries.summary: Sixth family on the Phase 2 baseline. Pairs with CM (backup_strategy in §6) and IR (recovery phase).

entries.subject: feat(plans): IR family plan (Incident Response)
entries.summary: Fifth family on the Phase 2 baseline. Pairs with AU since incidents are detected via the audit pipeline.

entries.subject: feat(plans): IA family plan + multi-select template substitution fix
entries.summary: Fourth family on the Phase 2 baseline. Pairs with AC since AC delegates the underlying authenticator strength and identity proofing to IA.

entries.subject: feat(plans): AU family plan (Audit and Accountability)
entries.summary: Third family on the Phase 2 baseline. Pure schema work — same pattern as AC.

entries.subject: feat(plans): AC family plan + wizard badge clarity fix
entries.summary: First family added on top of the Phase 2 baseline. Pure schema work — no engine changes needed — confirming the schema-driven design pays off on family expansion.

entries.subject: feat(plans): Phase 2 — assessability (ODVs, tailoring, structured CM)
entries.summary: Real-RMF-practitioner feedback on the Phase 1 CM Plan flagged 20 assessability gaps: the plan was structurally sound but lacked the enforceable, measurable, organization-defined parameters that ATO evidence requires. Phase 2 closes those gaps and establishes the new assessability floor for every future family schema.

entries.subject: feat(plans): schema-driven family-plan generator (Phase 1, CM-first)
entries.summary: A wizard-based generator that produces NIST RMF family compliance plans (Configuration Management Plan first; AC, AU, IR, etc. follow as schema-only effort).

entries.subject: perf(search): shard docs.json to bring per-search memory under 256M
entries.summary: Replaces the single 154 MB docs.json (which parsed to ~400 MB PHP array on every search) with a directory of fixed-size shard files, 1000 docs per shard. The store loads only the shards that contain matched doc indexes, so a typical query touches a handful of shards (~3-5 MB each) instead of the full corpus.

entries.subject: fix(search): bump memory_limit on search path so 256M hosts don't OOM
entries.summary: A search currently loads the entire 154 MB docs.json into a PHP array (~400 MB resident, ~544 MB peak during JSON decode) plus postings and trigrams. Production was hitting "Allowed memory size of 268435456 bytes exhausted" - PHP's default 256M cap is below the working set.

entries.subject: fix(search): bump memory_limit in IndexBuilder so rebuild runs OOTB
entries.summary: The full rebuild walks ~1.2 GB of STIG XML and holds the postings, docs, and trigram tables in memory simultaneously, peaking around 1.5-2 GB. Default php.ini memory_limit (often 128M-512M) trips a fatal during the build, both from the CLI command and from the post-DISA-pull auto-rebuild hook in the controllers.

entries.subject: fix(stig): default released date to '' when 'Date:' missing
entries.summary: explode('Date:', \$released)[1] threw 'Undefined array key 1' for STIGs whose release-info plain-text didn't contain 'Date:' (or had an empty release-info). Surfaced on /stig listing — STIGs without the substring crashed the loop.

entries.subject: fix(twig): guard xpath|first chains against empty results
entries.summary: Twig 3.18+ tightened attribute access: |first on an empty array yields false (PHP current([])), and accessing an attribute on a bool now errors instead of silently returning null/empty. Three templates (stig, scap, rmf v5) chained .references / .title onto xpath()|first results without checking, which broke when the looked-up CCI or related RMF control wasn't in the loaded XML data.
